title: Two contractor names, one telephone, email or set of officers
question: Do City contract notices filed for differently named contractors give the same telephone, email domain, suite or officers?
finding: 1,725 contractors appear on 99,274 notice rows. 491 pairs whose names are alike were set aside as one family by name; of the rest, 317 pairs of differently named contractors give the same telephone, company email domain or suite. 26 pairs are already one owner-group in the owner-groups screen and 23 are joint ventures or law-firm teams. 22 pairs of City payees are left that no other screen ties together, 12 of them on two or more kinds of shared detail (32 further pairs involve a project or housing company). The strongest: Crestwood Behavioral Health Inc. ($173.3 million paid since fiscal 2019) and Helios Healthcare LLC ($24.7 million): the same telephone; the same email domain (cbhi.net); 4 identically named officers or owners.
how: Every contract that an elected official or the Board approves needs a notice to the Ethics Commission (Form 126) naming the contractor, its address, telephone and email, and its officers, directors, owners of 10% or more and subcontractors. Both files of notices (2018 to 2026) are read; contractor names are grouped on the project name key. A notice name is tied to the Controller's payee name when the keys are equal, when the payee name is the same words abbreviated, or by its trade name. Two contractors are paired when they give the same telephone, the same company email domain, the same suite, or at least 5 officers or owners with the same first and last name. Telephones that the notices also give for a City filer or department contact, free-mail and City email domains, and any value given by more than 6 names are not used. Pairs already in one owner-group (the “aliases” analysis) or alike by name are counted and left out. Payments are the Controller's payment file since fiscal 2019, matched on the name key.
limits: A shared telephone, domain or board is what a parent and its subsidiary, a sponsor and its project company, a merger or a shared bookkeeper look like, and all of those are ordinary. The notice is typed by City staff or the contractor and can carry the wrong telephone. Officers are compared by first and last name only and are not named here; where nothing else is shared the notices do not show whether they are the same people (the organizations' tax returns or Secretary of State statements would). Payments are matched by name and can miss a payee paid under another spelling.
